item.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
item.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. item.title: Ogun ready for State Police – Abiodun
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun has declared his administration’s readiness to establish a state police force, describing it as a critical step towards strengthening security, protecting investments and sustaining the state’s growing economic activities. The governor also announced the immediate commencement of a social investment cash transfer programme for vulnerable residents to cushion the effects of rising food and transportation costs. Abiodun made the announcements at a town hall meeting on the 2027 budget and the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for Remo Division, held at the Akarigbo Palace, Sagamu. Speaking on the proposed establishment of state police, the governor, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police, said Ogun was prepared to embrace the initiative, noting that the state’s expanding industrial and commercial activities required a more robust security framework. He declared: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police creation. Ogun State is ready for state police.” Abiodun said his administration had consistently strengthened the state’s security architecture through the provision of operational vehicles, allowances and equipment, as well as increased recruitment into the Ogun State Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun. He disclosed that Amotekun and the So-Safe Corps currently had a combined strength of about 6,000 personnel. “To protect the gains we have made, we have continued to strengthen our security architecture by providing them with vehicles, allowances and equipment. We have empowered our Amotekun and increased their recruitment,” he said. On the cash transfer initiative, the governor said the programme was designed to provide direct financial support to vulnerable households grappling with the rising cost of living, particularly food and transportation. He linked the prevailing economic pressures partly to disruptions in the global oil and gas supply chain arising from the ongoing Israel-American-Iran conflict, which he said had contributed to rising oil prices and transportation costs. “We are going to start the implementation of our social investment cash initiative. We are going to transfer cash to our people to cushion the effects of this America-Israel-Iran war,” he stated. The governor disclosed that the programme would commence immediately in Sagamu, with beneficiaries already identified and captured in the state’s database expected to receive payment alerts. He added that the initiative would subsequently be extended to other communities across Remoland and the entire state. “I am starting that today in Sagamu. I’m going into Ogijo from here. All those who have been generated to benefit will get their alerts today while I’m there. I’m going to do the same across Remoland and of course, the whole state,” he said. item.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to shut down substandard CBT centres
item.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination. item.title: British woman, unborn baby die in Nigeria; family seeks help to bring bodies home
item.description: A 40-year-old British woman who relocated to Nigeria to start a new life with her husband has died alongside her unborn baby after developing sepsis. Claire Chadwick, who was 37 weeks pregnant, reportedly suffered septic shock after her baby girl died in the womb. In a report by Daily Mail UK, Chadwick had moved to Nigeria to be with her husband, Ibrahim, and was expecting their first child together. She had built a social media following of thousands through videos documenting their relationship, religious beliefs and food challenges on TikTok and Instagram. Her death has left her family devastated, with her sister, Shannon, revealing that she is survived by her 19-year-old son in Wales, her husband and other relatives. Describing her late sister, Shannon said Claire was a funny and fiercely strong-minded woman who lived life on her own terms. “She was a woman who lived her life in her own way and she will leave a lasting impression on everyone who knew her,” she told WalesOnline. The family has since launched a GoFundMe campaign with a target of £10,000 to repatriate Claire and her unborn daughter to the United Kingdom for burial. Explaining the purpose of the fundraiser, Shannon said the family wanted to bring both bodies home so they could be laid to rest with dignity and surrounded by their loved ones. “More than anything, we want them both returned so they can be laid to rest with dignity, surrounded by the family who love them,” she said. The fundraiser has attracted widespread support, with Shannon describing the response as overwhelming. She also expressed gratitude to REST, a charity that supports families dealing with the sudden or tragic deaths of loved ones abroad. Tributes have also poured in from friends and well-wishers, who remembered Chadwick as a kind, caring and cheerful woman. One supporter recalled knowing her from childhood and described her as lovely, while another said she was devastated by the loss, remembering her as someone who always made people laugh. The family hopes to raise enough money to bring Claire and her unborn daughter back to the UK. item.title: ADC crisis: No one is above party constitution, Nafiu Bala tells Mark-led exco
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe, National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has declared that no political party leader is above the party’s constitution, following the Federal High Court judgment on the party’s leadership dispute. Gombe said the judgment reinforced the principle that leadership positions in political parties must emerge through lawful and constitutionally recognised procedures, not imposition or political expediency, insisting that courts must intervene when parties disregard their own rules. In a statement reacting to the judgment in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, involving him, the ADC and four others, Gombe commended the trial judge for what he described as an independent, impartial and courageous handling of the politically sensitive dispute. “With profound respect for the Bench, and with a deep sense of duty to the administration of justice in Nigeria, I most respectfully commend the Federal High Court and the trial Judge for the independent, impartial, and intellectually rigorous manner in which His Lordship handled and determined the above-referenced matter,” he said. Describing the case as a major test of judicial independence, Gombe said it raised critical questions about party autonomy, internal democracy, constitutional supremacy and the regulatory responsibilities of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). “By subjecting the question of leadership emergence to constitutional and statutory scrutiny, rather than to political expediency, His Lordship affirmed a foundational principle of Nigerian jurisprudence: political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not a mere suggestion,” he stated. On the obligation of political parties to obey their internal rules, Gombe said courts had a duty to intervene where established procedures were disregarded. “Where a party’s constitution prescribes a procedure for succession and leadership, that procedure must be obeyed. Where a political party fails to comply with the rules, procedures, and constitutional provisions laid down for its own governance, the court is duty-bound to intervene in order to safeguard democracy, uphold the rule of law, and prevent anarchy. “No man is above the law, and no man is below it,” he declared. The ADC chairman said the judgment went beyond the immediate contest between the parties, arguing that it demonstrated that the judiciary could withstand political pressure and decide cases strictly on their merits. “It restores public confidence that a judge can still decide on the law and the facts alone, uninfluenced by political pressure, media commentary, or the weight of personalities involved in the suit. “It affirms that leadership must emerge through lawful process, not through imposition, and that aggrieved members have a legitimate right to seek redress in court rather than resort to self-help. item.title: Zidane’s son dropped from Algeria squad for AFCON qualifiers
item.description: Algeria goalkeeper Luca Zidane was left out of the national team squad on Thursday ahead of two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Togo, coach Brahim Hemdani said. Zidane, 28, has recently been missing from the Algerian team, owing to injury and a two-game suspension over scuffles during an AFCON game against Nigeria in January. But his exclusion was “based on sporting criteria”, Hemdani told journalists. “I need to have three goalkeepers who were getting as much playing time as possible.” Hemdani called up USM Alger goalkeeper Oussama Benbot alongside Melvin Mastil of Swiss club Lausanne-Sport and Abdelatif Ramdane of MC Alger. Zidane, a son of French football icon Zinedine Zidane, joined the Fennecs after changing his sporting nationality in September 2025 to represent Algeria, where his family has roots. The Leganes goalkeeper’s absence came as a surprise, along with that of Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri. Ait-Nouri had been sent home in September following a reported dispute with the coaching staff during a match against Zambia. But Hemdani said there had been “no problem” after his choice not to include the left-back in his next 26-man squad, adding that there were “criteria for inclusion”. “However, anything is possible in the future, and no one has been permanently excluded,” the coach said. Algeria are set to face Togo on November 14 and 17. They have four points from two games and are currently top of AFCON qualification Group I, which includes Zambia and Burundi. item.title: Nigerian teenager, Fawaz jailed four years for attempting to steal Porsche in London
item.description: A 19-year-old Nigerian teenager, Fawaz Oyedeji, has been sentenced to four years in prison in the United Kingdom for attempting to steal a £72,500 Porsche Cayenne using an imitation firearm. Oyedeji, who is from Greenwich, London, posed as a prospective buyer after responding to an online advertisement for the luxury sports utility vehicle. He arranged to meet the seller at the victim’s home in Southwark on Tuesday, March 18, to inspect the vehicle. After the victim showed him around the Porsche, the pair entered the front seats to discuss the sale. Oyedeji then produced what appeared to be a firearm, pointed it at the seller and demanded the car keys. However, the victim resisted and fought back, forcing Oyedeji to abandon the attempt and flee from the scene. The police were subsequently alerted and launched an investigation into the incident. Detectives traced the phone used to arrange the vehicle inspection to Oyedeji, establishing that it had been in the vicinity of both his home address and the scene of the attempted robbery. Investigators also obtained CCTV footage showing his movements shortly before and after the incident. Clothing matching what the suspect wore during the attempted robbery was also recovered by officers. Oyedeji was arrested at his home on Leonard Robbins Path within 38 hours of the offence. A jury at the Inner London Crown Court found him guilty after just 26 minutes of deliberation on Wednesday, November 4. He was subsequently sentenced to four years’ imprisonment. Detective Constable Alex Long, who led the investigation, praised the victim for resisting the armed robbery and cooperating with investigators. “The victim showed immense courage by refusing to hand over his keys despite being threatened with what appeared to be a genuine firearm,” Long said. He added that CCTV footage, digital records and forensic evidence helped detectives build a strong case that secured Oyedeji’s conviction. The detective also urged people buying or selling vehicles privately to take necessary precautions, advising them to leave if a transaction appeared suspicious and call emergency services when necessary. item.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists. Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. “All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said. He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed. “Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said. Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern. “Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said. The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election. “I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked. Wike further questioned whether Obi still enjoyed the level of financial and popular support associated with his 2023 presidential campaign. “The Obi wave is dead and buried. How many people are contributing money for Obi today?” he said. The post 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well
item.description: Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process. Bwala made the remarks in a post on his X platform on Thursday, following the controversy surrounding the leadership of the opposition party. He said a political party seeking to govern Nigeria must uphold the principles of due process, equity and justice, accusing the Mark-led executive of disregarding those principles in its emergence. “A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice. “You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well,” he wrote. Bwala further accused the leadership of violating the party’s constitution and guidelines, as well as the Nigerian Constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said the alleged violations amounted to a disregard for Nigerians, accusing the party leadership of assuming that the public could be misled over the circumstances surrounding its emergence. Bwala also took a swipe at individuals lobbying on behalf of the party leadership, suggesting that they were expecting financial rewards. The comments came amid the dispute over the ADC leadership and a court ruling affecting the Mark-led executive committee. item.title: Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as court sacks Mark-led ADC exco
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP. While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu , declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party. The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought. The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State. Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. item.title: No child is useless, every child is ordained for greatness — Foluke Adeboye
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The wife of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Foluke Adeboye, has called on parents, churches, governments and other stakeholders to take greater responsibility for raising children with godly character and values, saying Nigeria’s future depends on how its young people are nurtured. Adeboye made the call in her welcome address, titled “The Mandate of Kingdom Education in National Transformation,” at the annual summit of Christ The Redeemer’s School Management (CRSM), a multidimensional ministry of the RCCG, held at Redemption City of God along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The summit was themed “Revisiting Kingdom Education: The Role of Stakeholders.” She said the responsibility for effective Christian education begins at home, urging parents to train their children properly and cooperate with teachers in shaping their character. Adeboye cautioned parents against over-pampering their children during school holidays, urging them to allow the young ones to grow in accordance with godly values. “Every child must fear God because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. We see many of these children that look down on their teachers. If parents discharge their duties effectively, it will make the teacher’s work easier. Meditate on God’s word day and night,” she said. She also urged parents not to shy away from correcting their children, stressing that discipline and proper upbringing were essential to national development. “If only everyone of us can come together, do the right things, raise our children rightly, the success of Nigeria is in our hands,” she added. Adeboye further charged children to obey their parents and called on churches to teach sound biblical doctrines. She urged leaders to discharge their responsibilities diligently and exercise sound judgment, warning that failure to provide responsible leadership could create room for corruption, criminality and other social vices. On the role of government, she called for the provision of adequate structures and learning facilities in schools, particularly in rural communities where, she said, some pupils still sit on the floor because of a lack of chairs. She noted that such schools were often upgraded through evangelism and missionary activities because of the need to address the challenges confronting rural education. “So many things are wrong and these children from the village have great destiny to fulfil. God is counting on them. They brought David from the bush to be a king of Israel. No child is a useless child; God ordained every child to be great. I believe by the time I leave, I must have made substantial impact over the education in this nation,” she said. item.title: Tinubu saved Nigeria from turning to Venezuela — Emerhor
item.description: A founding leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor, has declared that Nigeria would have suffered an economic collapse similar to Venezuela’s if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not demonstrated the courage and foresight to introduce far-reaching economic reforms upon assuming office in 2023. Olorogun Emerhor, who stated this on Thursday during the Delta State APC campaign flag-off in Oleh, Isoko South Local Government Area, said Tinubu inherited an economy weakened by years of poor management and unsustainable policies, insisting that the President’s difficult but necessary decisions had rescued the country from the brink of economic disaster. The APC chieftain also called for the re-election of President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in 2027, arguing that both leaders had demonstrated the capacity to reposition the country and state for sustainable economic growth and infrastructural transformation. According to Emerhor, Nigeria was heading towards an economic crisis comparable to that of Venezuela, an oil-rich South American country that experienced severe economic difficulties despite possessing some of the world’s largest crude oil reserves. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rescued Nigeria. If our President had not taken those bold decisions, Nigeria would have gone the way of Venezuela. Do you want Nigeria to become another Venezuela? “Venezuela has more oil than Nigeria, but bad leadership and years of economic mismanagement destroyed its economy. For many years, that was the kind of governance we experienced in Nigeria,” he stated. Emerhor criticised some opposition political figures seeking to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that several of them were part of the political establishment responsible for the country’s longstanding economic difficulties. He maintained that it took Tinubu’s political courage and determination to confront the structural challenges that previous administrations had failed to address. “All those who are today running to become President were part of the system that contributed to the destruction of Nigeria. It was Bola Ahmed Tinubu who had the courage to take those difficult decisions. “Today, we are beginning to have a stable economy. The President has laid a strong foundation for economic prosperity. We have a prudent President, and our foreign reserves are growing. Tinubu is doing well,” Emerhor declared. The APC leader argued that removing Tinubu after his first term would amount to abandoning the economic recovery process midway, stressing that the President deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms and deliver their anticipated benefits to Nigerians. item.title: ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has criticised the court ruling nullifying the African Democratic Congress (ADC) executive committee and its candidates, alleging that the development could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in Nigeria. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties. CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state. The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation. The statement read in part: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.” It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process. CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system. The coalition warned that the judiciary must remain guided by the Constitution and the interests of Nigerians rather than political considerations. “The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement said. CUPP declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism. The coalition added: “CUPP stands in solidarity with the ADC and all progressive forces in Nigeria. We will not sit idly by while the hard-earned democratic gains of our nation are plundered by an authoritarian regime.” The post ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSC posts four commissioners of police to states
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of four Commissioners of Police to Plateau, Enugu, Nasarawa and Ondo states following interviews to assess their suitability for the new assignments. The commission’s spokesman, Torty Njoku, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday at the Solomon Arase Conference Hall, PSC headquarters, Abuja. The newly posted commissioners are CP Sunday J. A. Okoebor, formerly Commissioner of Police, Police Accounts and Budget, Force Headquarters, who has been posted to Plateau State. Others are CP Fidelis Ogarabe, formerly Commissioner of Police, INTERPOL Annex, Lagos, posted to Enugu State; CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, formerly Commissioner of Police, Force Intelligence Annex, Lagos, posted to Nasarawa State; and CP Johnson Ayodeji Babalola, formerly Commissioner of Police, Special Inquiry, Force Headquarters, Abuja, posted to Ondo State. The Chairman of the commission, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu, who affirmed the postings, said they were in line with Section 215(1)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which empowers the commission to appoint Commissioners of Police for each state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory. Argungu, who was represented by a board member, Hon. Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC rtd.), said the officers had demonstrated the requisite knowledge and character during the interviews. He urged them to discharge their responsibilities with impartiality and live up to the expectations of their new offices. item.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, improve security and create employment if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge on Thursday during a campaign rally in Kebbi State, where he called on voters to support the ADC, describing it as the only party committed to addressing the three issues. “The people of Kebbi State, let me ask you a few questions. Do you want the return of subsidy? Do you want security? Do you want employment? Therefore you have no option other than the ADC. ADC is the only political party that is committed to these three objectives and more to bring about prosperity, unity and peace to the people of our country,” he said. The former Vice President and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the President Bola Tinubu administration, describing them as legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. Supporters of the ADC gathered at the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party faithful for what he described as their resistance to intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 general elections would be a referendum between suffering Nigerians and the Federal Government under President Tinubu. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that no amount of intimidation could stop. He called on the people of Kebbi State to vote for Atiku as president, Abubakar Malami as governor and other ADC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The rally ended with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Crowd at Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign rally in Kebbi. The campaign in Kebbi came hours after a Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the Senator David Mark-led ADC and voided the actions taken by the party’s executives, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku rejected the ruling, describing it as an attempt to weaken his political support and frustrate his campaign. He said he would challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The ADC also rejected the decision, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to cripple the opposition and vowing to challenge the judgment through all available judicial processes. item.title: Saudi Arabia executes five Ethiopians for hashish smuggling
item.description: Saudi Arabia has executed five Ethiopian nationals convicted of drug smuggling, bringing the kingdom’s execution toll this year to 205, according to the country’s Interior Ministry. The five were convicted of participating in smuggling hashish into the kingdom, the ministry said in a statement published by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday. They were executed in Asir, a province in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The latest executions are the third such announcement involving Ethiopian nationals in recent months. Five Ethiopians were executed on the same day in June, while another five were put to death in July. With the latest executions, 32 Ethiopian nationals have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, making them the largest foreign national group among those executed. Human Rights Watch warned in July that at least 79 Ethiopians faced an imminent risk of execution over similar drug-related charges. Saudi Arabia recorded 356 executions last year, the highest annual figure in the kingdom’s history. Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia, with many travelling to the oil-rich kingdom through the perilous Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa via Yemen. item.title: Atiku flags off ADC campaign in Kebbi, pledges security, fuel subsidy restoration
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to address Nigeria’s security challenges and restore fuel subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the promises during the flag-off of his campaign in Kebbi State, where he described the forthcoming election as a referendum on the policies of the President Bola Tinubu administration. He said the election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to decide whether to retain the current government or embrace an alternative amid concerns over economic hardship and insecurity. Supporters of the ADC converged on the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the campaign rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party members for attending the gathering despite what he described as intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 election would be a referendum on the performance of the Tinubu administration, adding that hunger, insecurity and unemployment would feature prominently in the campaign. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that could not be stopped by intimidation. He urged Kebbi residents to vote for Abubakar Malami as governor, Atiku as president and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Atiku and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the Tinubu administration, alleging that they were legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. They described the ADC as an alternative for Nigerians seeking improved security and a reversal of the fuel subsidy policy. The rally climaxed with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Meanwhile, security was heightened in Birnin Kebbi ahead of Atiku’s arrival, with security personnel deployed across parts of the state capital to prevent any breakdown of law and order. The campaign rally ended peacefully, with no reported attacks or destruction of vehicles, unlike the violence alleged to have accompanied the party’s campaign activities in Sokoto State. item.title: Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their 3-1 victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. In a statement issued by his media aide, Bayo Onanuga, the President described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. Tinubu also commended the coaching crew and everyone whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urged the players to remain focused, confident and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill and unwavering support of Nigerians. “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. President Bola Tinubu The Flamingos reached the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after defeating Brazil 3-1 in their semi-final encounter in Morocco. The Nigerian girls produced a spirited second-half performance, scoring three goals before Brazil grabbed a late consolation. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute, finishing off an assist from Oluwakemi Adegubyi to give Nigeria the lead. The Flamingos doubled their advantage in the 71st minute when Awawu Bashiru found the net, with Joseph providing the assist. Bashiru struck again in the 80th minute to make it 3-0, converting a pass from Oluebube Umejiaku as Nigeria took firm control of the encounter. Brazil pulled one back in the 89th minute through Greise Kelly, assisted by Yasmin Queiroz, but the goal came too late to prevent Nigeria from securing victory and a place in the final. item.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesters take part in a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Bordeaux on November 5, 2026. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. School blockades Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. French police officers march amid the smoke during a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks, in Nantes on November 5, 2026.
